title: Rabbi Ada of Yafo

paragraphs: Taanit 9b as cited by Hyman (the named passage is at [16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.16b.15)) mentions him explaining Rabbi Yehudah’s reasoning. In [Megillah 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.16b.10) he says that the names of Haman’s ten sons and the words “and the ten” must be recited in one breath. The [Rif](https://www.sefaria.org/Rif_Megillah.4a.6) and [Rosh](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_on_Megillah.1.9.1) read Rabbi Abba of Yafo.

We also find Rabbi Chiya, son of Rabbi Ada of Yafo, in [Bereshit Rabbah 38:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.38.13) and [Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Moed_Katan.3.7.14).[^3]

notes.text: The Rif and Rosh form is Abba, whereas the supplied heading and the son’s patronym use Ada.
The consulted Gemara names Rav Ada of Yafo. The consulted Rif and Rosh texts give Rabbi Abba of Yafo. All three give the instruction to say the names and “and the ten” in one breath.

[Heilprin’s Ada entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=218&lang=en) cites Taanit 16b, where Ada explains Rabbi Yehudah’s view about the prayers for a public fast. His explanation [continues on 17a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.17a.1). The two linked sources for Chiyya differ: the consulted Bereshit Rabbah calls him Ada’s grandson, while the Yerushalmi calls him Ada’s son. See also [Heilprin’s Chiyya entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1234&lang=en).
